exemplar: Hamilton argues that the American founding is a test case for all humanity: whether people can create good government through reasoned deliberation and choice, rather than having constitutions imposed by accident or force.

The Articles of Confederation's weakness - Congress could not tax, regulate commerce, or enforce its laws, as Shays's Rebellion exposed - convinced Hamilton and others that a stronger national government was necessary.
The ratification debate produced the Bill of Rights (1791): Anti-Federalist demands for explicit protections of individual liberty were answered with the first ten amendments.
parts: A. Briefly describe Hamilton's claim about the significance of the American founding in the excerpt.
B. Briefly explain ONE weakness of the government under the Articles of Confederation that the Constitution was meant to address.
C. Briefly explain ONE way the ratification debate shaped the final form of the Constitution's government.

stimulus.attribution: Alexander Hamilton, Federalist No. 1, October 27, 1787 (Founders Online, National Archives).
stimulus.text: It has been frequently remarked that it seems to have been reserved to the people of this country, by their conduct and example, to decide the important question, whether societies of men are really capable or not of establishing good government from reflection and choice, or whether they are forever destined to depend for their political constitutions on accident and force.

exemplar: The photograph shows an ordinary worker performing skilled, dangerous industrial labor - humanizing the factory workforce that Progressive reformers sought to protect.
Reformers responded with state and federal labor laws: workers' compensation statutes, limits on working hours, and the Keating-Owen Child Labor Act (1916) all aimed to curb industrial exploitation.
The Supreme Court limited these reforms in cases like Lochner v. New York (1905) and Hammer v. Dagenhart (1918), striking down labor laws as violations of liberty of contract or of federalism.
parts: A. Briefly describe what the photograph shows about industrial work in the early twentieth century.
B. Briefly explain ONE way reformers attempted to address the conditions shown in the photograph.
C. Briefly explain ONE way the Supreme Court limited Progressive labor reforms.

stimulus.text: The photograph shows a power house mechanic - an adult worker in overalls - straining to operate a massive steam pump in an industrial plant. The machinery dwarfs him; grease, heat, and physical danger are evident in the close, dark composition.
